work: Round 2 T5 — the six untested claims, verified directly rather than delegated
principle: Each claim was RESOLVED by measurement or by an authoritative dated source. None is left as an assumption.

1_DIARIZATION_CEILING.status: RESOLVED — round 2 was right, my 50 was wrong
1_DIARIZATION_CEILING.authoritative_source: https://developers.deepgram.com/reference/api-rate-limits.md, Pay As You Go section, fetched 2026-10-15
1_DIARIZATION_CEILING.quote_model_row: Nova-3 | Europe | Pre-Recorded Up to 50 concurrent requests
1_DIARIZATION_CEILING.quote_diarization_row: Speaker Diarization | Europe | Pre-Recorded Up to 25 concurrent requests | Streaming Up to 25 concurrent requests
1_DIARIZATION_CEILING.quote_precedence: If multiple services are used in one API call (e.g Speech to Text + Sentiment Analysis), the lower of the rate limits is applied.
1_DIARIZATION_CEILING.reasoning: diarize=true is NON-OPTIONAL for this build: section 10.1 requires `speakers` to be diarisation clusters, and Rule 3 forbids removing the capability. So the request uses both features and the LOWER limit applies: min(50, 25) = 25.
1_DIARIZATION_CEILING.plan_value: TRANSCRIBE_CONCURRENCY = 16, which is under the binding ceiling with 60% headroom
1_DIARIZATION_CEILING.how_the_error_happened: The concurrency probe corrected a stale 25 to 50 by reading the MODEL table and silently substituting it for the DIARIZATION table. Round 2 caught the substitution. The original 25 in the eu-limits artifact was correct all along, and I doubted a correct value because a newer-looking number existed.
1_DIARIZATION_CEILING.also_confirmed: 'Rate limits apply per project, not per account or API key.' A second account adds budget, not throughput — as previously recorded.

2_WORST_CASE_SUBMISSION.unit: dvcEDToK — the longest call in the corpus, 204.3 min
2_WORST_CASE_SUBMISSION.submitted: 280.7 MB remuxed .mka, the path the plan actually takes
2_WORST_CASE_SUBMISSION.result: HTTP 200 in 103.2 s; upload 1.9 s at 150.8 MB/s; total 105.1 s against a 600 s ceiling
2_WORST_CASE_SUBMISSION.superseded: the calculated 273.7x, which was wrong by 48x

3_STEREO_DURATION_SEMANTICS.status: RESOLVED — benign for the gates, with one residual
3_STEREO_DURATION_SEMANTICS.method: a 120 s STEREO clip and a 120 s MONO clip of the same corpus audio, submitted identically, duration compared against decoded PCM length
3_STEREO_DURATION_SEMANTICS.what_round_2_predicted: That Deepgram reports DOUBLED duration for stereo, breaking COMMIT_COST != SETTLE_FROM and guaranteeing V12 clause 6's 2% reconcile fails on every preserved stereo part.
3_STEREO_DURATION_SEMANTICS.verdict_on_that: NOT CONFIRMED. Stereo reports 1.00x true duration. The money gate does not break and the reconcile holds.

THE_RESIDUAL_ROUND_2_MISSED.finding: The response reports 1 channel and 1x duration for a STEREO input, while Deepgram's own pricing states stereo is billed at 2x ('a 10-minute file with 2 channels is billed for 20 minutes').
THE_RESIDUAL_ROUND_2_MISSED.consequence: The receipt UNDER-RECORDS the bill by 2x on any kept-stereo unit. SETTLE_FROM as written would capture 1x while the card is charged 2x.
THE_RESIDUAL_ROUND_2_MISSED.fix: settle = metadata.duration x (INPUT channel count, from the local part, never from the response's channel array). The response cannot be trusted for this because it collapses to 1 channel.
THE_RESIDUAL_ROUND_2_MISSED.exposure: Small — section 7.1a measured 3 of 3 stereo files as dual-mono, so the KEEP-STEREO branch measured 0 of 3. But the branch exists and the gate must be correct on it.

4_ADMISSION_ARITHMETIC_VS_THE_LARGEST_UN.round_2_claimed: A 3.00 GB unit named '10-03-2024 ... October Reading Offers Call - 1476x10' is permanently unfetchable under the 2x-declared admission rule.

what_the_manifest_actually_holds.largest_declared_in_manifest: 2,048 MiB — and it is a SENTINEL, not a measurement
what_the_manifest_actually_holds.where_round_2_got_it: The older deepgram-eu-limits evidence artifact, not the current manifest. The artifact is stale on this point.
what_the_manifest_actually_holds.sentinels_in_scope: 73 of 230 units, whose true sizes are unknown to a +/-0.5 quantum display band
what_the_manifest_actually_holds.measured_example: dvcEDToK declared 2 GiB, actually 1,614,043,424 bytes = 1.50 GiB

the_real_constraint_is_worse_than_round_.conclusion: FETCH_CONCURRENCY = 6 is UNSATISFIABLE for large units — 6 x 2560 = 15,360 MiB against 3,936 usable. W0-Cap proved the cap EXISTS; it never proved that any fixed concurrency is ADMISSIBLE across a corpus spanning 20 MiB to 2 GiB.
the_real_constraint_is_worse_than_round_.fix: FETCH_CONCURRENCY is not a constant. Admission becomes a size-adaptive predicate: admit(next) iff free >= sum(in_flight real_bytes) + real_bytes(next) + 64 MiB. That yields 1 in flight for large units and up to 39 for small ones, from one rule.
the_real_constraint_is_worse_than_round_.additional_requirement: Admission must use REAL bytes. For the 73 sentinels the real size is unknown until fetched, so reserve the display band's upper bound (2,560 MiB for a 2 GiB quantum), not the declared value.

5_FULL_DUPLEX_STREAMING_UPLOAD.status: PARTIALLY RESOLVED — bounded, one gap remains
5_FULL_DUPLEX_STREAMING_UPLOAD.what_was_proven: The remuxed 280.7 MB .mka streams and returns cleanly. The raw 1,539 MB MP4 did not complete (>1800 s), and the difference was NOT bandwidth — the remuxed file uploaded at 150.8 MB/s, so 1.5 GB is ~10 s of transfer. The difference is that -vn strips the h264 VIDEO TRACK.
5_FULL_DUPLEX_STREAMING_UPLOAD.what_this_proves_strongly: The remux is MANDATORY, not an optimisation. 133 of 230 units are MP4, and under Constraint 7 a failed submission is paid and unrecoverable.

the_remaining_gap.gap: The largest REMUXED unit in scope has not been submitted.
the_remaining_gap.estimate: The largest source is a 2 GiB sentinel; measured MP4 size cut is ~80%, so the largest remuxed unit is ~400 MB against the 280.7 MB proven.
the_remaining_gap.risk: Moderate. The proven case had 5.7x time headroom, and upload at 150.8 MB/s means 400 MB is ~2.7 s of transfer.
the_remaining_gap.mitigation: If a remuxed part exceeds 500 MB, segment it at SEGMENT_SEC rather than discovering the threshold in production. The segmentation path already exists and its removal was a round-2 correction, so this reintroduces it as a size guard rather than a fallback.

6_STEREO_SAVING_EXTRAPOLATION.status: RESOLVED — the budget gap is now explicit
6_STEREO_SAVING_EXTRAPOLATION.finding: The $26.98 saving came from 10 files. The budget table in section 2.2 has NO line for the KEEP-STEREO branch, which bills 2x while reporting 1x (see #3).
6_STEREO_SAVING_EXTRAPOLATION.exposure: Bounded by measurement: 3 of 3 stereo files were dual-mono, so the keep branch fired 0 of 3. If it fires on every sampled unit instead, the cost is the full 2x on those units, and section 2.2's $150.56 was computed on 1x minutes.
fixes: settle multiplies by the INPUT channel count from the local part, never the response's channel array
section 2.2 gains an explicit keep-stereo line, sized as a worst case rather than omitted
the per-file (L-R) decision in 7.1a means the branch is evaluated per unit, so the exposure is discovered during the run rather than after it

METHOD_NOTE: Five of the six were closed by running something or reading an authoritative dated source. One (#5) is bounded rather than closed, and is recorded as bounded rather than described as safe. The pattern across all six: every one of them was a claim the plan stated in prose and no probe had ever touched.
